general.temas: Egyptian diplomacy and African cooperation are recurring themes, with particular attention to the Aswan Forum, as are regional conflicts in Yemen, Gaza and Sudan. Cultural, sports and service news also feature. Only Mada Masr highlights the proceedings against journalists and the order to shut down its own outlet.
general.motivo_crispacion: The tension stems from regional clashes, including threats between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia and allegations concerning Gaza. In Egypt, Mada Masr reports on opposition criticism of the parliamentary mandate to provide military support to Saudi Arabia, as well as arrests and proceedings against journalists. Concerns about Sudan’s security and Egypt’s water rights are also mentioned. News about diplomatic cooperation, culture, health and weather forecasts partly offsets this atmosphere.

Al-Masry Al-Youm.resumen:
- Egypt is seeking partnerships with Greece to access third markets, with a particular interest in Africa.
- Saudi Arabia warns that it will not tolerate aggression as Houthi threats expand.
- In Qena, a woman is accused of killing a young man and burning his body; the trial of the lawyer representing victims in a case involving the assault of minors is also reported.
- The front page covers Zamalek’s declining results and carries news about the Cairo International Film Festival and several entertainment figures.
- Details are provided on the mid-year school holidays and the early payment of pensions.
Al-Masry Al-Youm.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “fiery response” and “surprise”, together with shocking details of a crime, add sensationalism, although there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
Al-Masry Al-Youm.sesgo: The selection combines service news and official statements with a notable presence of sports and entertainment. No clear political bias is apparent in the headlines provided.

Youm7.resumen:
- The foreign minister reaffirms the defense of Egypt’s water interests and rights.
- The front page highlights diplomatic meetings and agreements with Sudan, Eritrea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as discussions on regional security and peace.
- Iran reports a visit by a Qatari delegation and two hours of talks.
- The health ministry identifies seven groups that need the seasonal flu vaccine.
- Fog, possible rain and temperature changes are forecast, and an opportunity to observe Mercury is reported.
Youm7.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although “no yielding on water rights” uses firm language and “temperature surprises” adds a sensationalist touch.
Youm7.sesgo: The selection prioritizes Egyptian diplomatic activity and official statements, with an emphasis on the country’s interests and security. Perspectives other than those of the authorities are barely represented.

Akhbar El-Yom.resumen:
- YouTube is nearing a $3 billion deal to settle lawsuits over “student addiction”; another headline warns about the effects of advertising on Egyptians’ wallets and health.
- At the Aswan Forum, President el-Sisi calls for reform of the international system and points to the impact of the global situation on Africa.
- The minister of solidarity highlights families’ transition from receiving aid to production and says 2.2 million families have left the “Takaful and Karama” program. The payment of public-sector salaries and children’s activities in 13 provinces are also reported.
- An academic conference on the tokatsu educational model opens, and 839 ration cards are seized in an inspection campaign in Giza.
- The front page carries results from the youth football World Cup, news about Barcelona players and the discovery of a sarcophagus documenting the life of a Yemeni merchant.
Akhbar El-Yom.motivo_populismo: Informative headlines predominate, although expressions such as “trade in illusions”, “trap” and “good news” add drama and emotional appeal.
Akhbar El-Yom.sesgo: The selection gives prominence to institutional activities and statements, presented mainly in terms of their stated objectives and results. The headline about advertising takes a critical and alarmist approach.

Al-Shorouk.resumen:
- Egypt’s foreign ministry says it is working to curb crises in neighboring countries and rejects interference in Sudan.
- Bahrain denounces new Iranian attacks at the UN; Iran unveils a dual missile launcher.
- Hamas calls for an urgent meeting over alleged Israeli violations in Gaza; Aoun identifies Israeli occupation and Iranian interference as obstacles to independence.
- In Yemen, the government reports military advances and the deaths of 260 children it says were recruited by the Houthis.
- The front page includes statements by Lieberman and Trump, priorities concerning archaeological heritage and an article about GTA 6.
Al-Shorouk.motivo_populismo: The reporting is predominantly attributed to sources, although expressions such as “playing with Sudan’s security” and “the hand of the Houthis” add drama and confrontation.
Al-Shorouk.sesgo: The selection prioritizes regional conflicts and statements by officials and political actors. Positions are mainly attributed to their sources, without the headlines including possible responses.

Mada Masr.resumen:
- The editor of Mada Masr is arrested after a fine of three million pounds and an order to shut down the outlet; the defense challenges two articles of the media law.
- The detention of all “Matsada2sh” journalists is extended by 15 days, according to a headline denouncing a lack of access and legal defense.
- A report examines damage to Palestinian olive groves in the context of war and occupation.
- Parliament authorizes the president to provide military support to Saudi Arabia; the opposition calls it a “blank check”.
- Litigation over the lands of St. Catherine’s Monastery is postponed, and talks with the IMF begin on the final review of the loan program.
Mada Masr.motivo_populismo: Informative headlines predominate, although expressions such as “no access, no defense” and “war on identity and resistance” use an emphatic and confrontational tone; “blank check” is attributed to the opposition.
Mada Masr.sesgo: The selection highlights proceedings against journalists and media outlets, with attention to safeguards for the defense. In the report on olive groves, the wording adopts a perspective sympathetic to Palestinians and presents Israeli actions as aggression.

opiniones.comunista:
I see two ways of understanding economic cooperation in today’s news. Egypt is seeking alliances with Greece to access third markets in Africa. I ask: who will decide the terms and who will receive the benefits? If they remain in the hands of big capital, commercial expansion will not be synonymous with progress for working people. I support agreements that guarantee labor rights, collective ownership and resources for public services.

I am also concerned by the announcement that 2.2 million families have left the Takaful and Karama program. The shift from aid to production will be progress only if those families have a decent income and social protection. And without a free press, citizens will struggle to scrutinize these decisions: the closure of Mada Masr and the arrest of its editor weaken that possibility.
opiniones.anarquista:
Today I am concerned by the distance between those who make decisions and those who bear the consequences. Egypt’s parliament has authorized the president to take measures to support Saudi Arabia against external aggression, as threats between Riyadh and the Houthis escalate. I do not trust a mandate concentrated at the top to protect communities better than cooperation among them. I reject escalation and stand for civilian solidarity over state rivalries.

I am also alarmed by the closure of Mada Masr and the arrest of its editor following a conviction for operating the website without a license. A free press should not depend on permission from those in power. In the face of the state, parties and hierarchies, I support self-managed media and mutual aid networks: individual freedom needs a free community to sustain it.
opiniones.liberal:
I welcome the pursuit of alliances between Egyptian and Greek companies to access other markets. Trade can open up opportunities that no ministerial plan can foresee. But for those alliances to work, I would reduce taxes and red tape for everyone, rather than distribute privileges through the state. Initiative and risk should remain in the hands of entrepreneurs, not taxpayers.

I am also concerned about the closure of Mada Masr and the arrest of its editor following a conviction for operating without a license. A free press should not need state permission to exist: it is indispensable for holding power to account. I support a limited state, able to protect rights and hold people accountable through the courts, but not to decide who can report the news. Without freedom of expression, there is no truly free market either.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I want a foreign policy that starts with Egypt, not with whatever commitments our elites see fit to make. Defending our water rights is essential: without water security, sovereignty is an empty word. That is why I would demand that every regional negotiation be judged by its results for Egyptians.

Parliament has authorized the president to take measures to support Saudi Arabia against external aggression. I understand the importance of regional security, but I do not accept a blank check: any military commitment must serve a specific national interest and be subject to oversight.

I also see opportunities in alliances with Greece to access third markets. Cooperation is sensible; dependence is not. Diplomacy must protect our ability to make our own decisions and the traditions that unite us, rather than asking the country to trust its leaders blindly.
opiniones.centro:
I am concerned about the closure of Mada Masr and the arrest of its editor following a conviction for operating the website without a license. Rules must be followed, but it must also be possible to challenge them in court. An independent press does not weaken the state: it holds it accountable and allows citizens to judge its decisions better. I hope the defense has access to the evidence and that an effective judicial review is guaranteed.

I also believe that support for Saudi Arabia requires clear limits and parliamentary oversight. Regional security matters, but a broad mandate should not replace public debate about its objectives and risks. I prefer sustained diplomacy, backed by accountable institutions, to decisions that commit the country without sufficient deliberation.
